storyTitle: India's Groundwater Crisis: 62% of Districts Sound the Alarm
editorialTier: Tier B — Solid with Minor Gaps
tierChangeRationale: CGWB 2022/23 assessment data verified (447.7 BCM recharge, 59.26% extraction rate); narrative requires clarification that 62% applies to NW agricultural districts rather than 62% of national assessment units.
domainFactCheckDetails: CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resource Assessment 2022/2023: Total annual groundwater recharge is 447.73 BCM. Annual extractable resource is 407.21 BCM. Annual groundwater extraction is 241.34 BCM (Stage of extraction: 59.26%). Assessment Units: 6,535 total units -> 1,134 over-exploited (17.35%), 699 critical (10.70%), 1,050 semi-critical (16.07%), 3,558 safe (54.44%). 62% figure applies to specific high-extraction districts in NW India (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan), NOT 62% of national assessment units.

authoritativeSources.exactTitle: Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India 2022/2023
authoritativeSources.issuingAuthority: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), Ministry of Jal Shakti
authoritativeSources.relevantPassageOrDataCell: Stage of groundwater extraction is 59.26% nationally; 17.35% of assessment units over-exploited.
authoritativeSources.caveats: Assessment units (blocks/mandals/talukas) must not be conflated with administrative districts.
